question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(ax), & 0<x\le 3 \\ 2x-6, & x>3\end{aligned}
$$

 
is continuous at  $x=3,$ find the value of $a.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=3,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}g(x) & =g(3)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3a),\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}(2x-6) \\  & =2(3)-6 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=3,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{+}}g(x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(3a) & =0 \\ 3a & =1 \\ a & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
